read: The US midterms dominated the tape. Democrats took both chambers, and the market read it as gridlock-positive: the NBI rose about 2% on Wednesday to within 1% of its 52-week high, though the XBI was more muted. Underneath, business development stayed heavy and China-weighted. Boehringer optioned six preclinical Sino Biopharm ADC/TCE programmes for $358m near-term and up to $7bn, and AbbVie paid $100m upfront for Nxera's gut-selective oral EP4 agonist. Single-asset risk cut both ways: Lyell rose 43% on clean pivotal CAR-T data, while Nurix fell about 38% when Sanofi dropped its STAT6 degrader, ahead of Kymera's key STAT6 readout. Overall the tone is risk-on, with capital still flowing to oral I&I, China-sourced oncology and obesity, and policy risk is shifting from drug pricing towards FDA oversight and PDUFA reauthorisation.

items.headline: Democrats win the House and Senate, and biopharma rallies.
items.detail: The NBI was up 2.1% intraday on 4 Nov (7,416), about 0.6% off its 52-week high. The XBI was roughly flat in morning trade. Analysts at Leerink, RBC and Jefferies expect little change to the IRA or the Trump-era MFN/tariff deals. The real lever is oversight: Bernie Sanders likely chairs HELP and so shapes PDUFA reauthorisation (the current law expires 30 Sept), and Heidi Overton's FDA commissioner nomination may lapse.

items.headline: Boehringer Ingelheim licenses six preclinical oncology programmes from Sino Biopharm for up to $7bn.
items.detail: The deal pays $358m upfront and near-term, with up to $7bn in option, development and commercial milestones plus royalties. The programmes are ADCs and T-cell engagers, five from LaNova and one from Beijing Tide. BI gets ex-China rights to four and worldwide rights to two, exercisable after clinical milestones. It is another heavily backloaded China option structure, and shows big pharma still buying China preclinical biologics despite the Treasury's COINS/outbound-investment noise.

items.headline: AbbVie licenses Nxera's oral EP4 agonist NXE0033744 for IBD for up to $1.47bn.
items.detail: AbbVie pays $100m upfront, plus up to $1.37bn in milestones and tiered royalties. The molecule is a gut-selective small molecule that has completed Phase 1, and it adds an oral, non-immunosuppressive mucosal-healing mechanism that could pair with Skyrizi and Rinvoq. Closing is subject to HSR.

items.headline: Lyell jumps 43% on ronde-cel pivotal data in large B-cell lymphoma.
items.detail: In the 3L+ PiNACLE trial, 44 patients were evaluable: ORR was 91% and CR 77%, 75% of CRs were maintained at 12 months, and 12-month PFS was 63%. There was no grade ≥3 CRS, and grade ≥3 ICANS was 9%. The 2L cohort (n=37) showed 95% ORR and 76% CR. Full pivotal data come in mid-2027, with a BLA in 2H27. This is a credible best-in-class CD19/CD20 autologous profile, though the trial is single-arm with short follow-up.

items.headline: Novo Nordisk raises 2026 guidance again on the Wegovy pill beat, and its CFO steps down.
items.detail: The Wegovy pill sold DKK 5.39bn (~$811m) in Q3, against DKK 4.96bn consensus. Adjusted sales and operating-profit growth guidance is now up to +2% at CER. The ADRs rose more than 6% in US trading. Karsten Munk Knudsen leaves at year-end and Galderma CFO Luigi La Corte replaces him. Novo says it won't launch CagriSema in Europe for "a couple of years". For comparison, Lilly's Foundayo did $184m in Q3. Update: the results were released early on 4 Nov; the new information is the market reaction and the call detail.

items.headline: Nurix falls about 38% after Sanofi drops the Phase 1 STAT6 degrader SAR448272.
items.detail: Sanofi cited emerging nonclinical findings in eczema, and Nurix loses future milestones. Leerink doesn't see a class read-through, and Sanofi keeps a separate STAT6 programme with Recludix. Even so, it raises the stakes for Kymera's KT-621 BROADEN2 Phase 2b readout.

items.headline: United Therapeutics pays Pfizer $525m to eliminate all ralinepag royalties.
items.detail: The royalty had been a low double-digit rate. Oral ralinepag is under FDA review for PAH with a PDUFA date of 24 Jun 2027. The buydown signals UTHR's confidence in the commercial size of the next-generation IP-receptor agonist.

items.headline: Spyre drops anti-TL1A SPY072 in rheumatology after SKYWAY Phase 2 misses.
items.detail: The drug missed its primary endpoints in PsA and axSpA, and the RA result was inconsistent across doses. Spyre is pivoting to hidradenitis suppurativa, with pivotal monotherapy studies planned for 2027. It is another data point that TL1A's value sits in IBD and HS rather than rheumatology.

items.headline: Madrigal faces a whistleblower suit alleging a Rezdiffra safety cover-up.
items.detail: The suit was filed by the company's former clinical development head, and plaintiff firms have opened investigations. It is headline risk for the leading MASH franchise just as GLP-1 competition intensifies.

items.headline: Ultragenyx cuts about 20% of staff and scraps its Wilson disease gene therapy.
items.detail: It is ending development of two rare-disease drugs after another failed study, an Angelman setback. Coming on top of earlier late-stage and regulatory setbacks, this is deep cost cutting. The news came out after the 3 Nov close.

items.headline: T-Therapeutics (Cambridge, UK) raises a $133m Series B.
items.detail: Advent Life Sciences and British Business Bank co-led, with Eli Lilly and J&J Innovation participating. The company makes TCR-CD3 bispecifics for cancer and autoimmunity and is heading into first-in-human studies. It is a large UK preclinical round with two strategics, which shows TCE-for-autoimmunity remains a magnet for capital.

items.headline: Ideaya closes the OptimUM-10 Phase 3 trial of darovasertib in neoadjuvant uveal melanoma.
items.detail: The company cited enrolment and site-activation problems. About $100–125m saved goes to IDE849 and IDE892, and the darovasertib NDA was filed in Q3. The shares were little changed (-1%). It is a quiet demotion of the Breakthrough-designated indication.

items.headline: Minghui licenses Japanese rights to its Phase 3 IGF-1R antibody MHB018A for thyroid eye disease to ASKA.
items.detail: ASKA pays $110m upfront, with up to $330m in milestones. That is a large upfront for a single-territory China out-licensing deal.

items.headline: Pfizer plans a Europe-first launch for its Lyme vaccine with Valneva (PF-07307405).
items.detail: The EMA filing was received in August, with a CHMP verdict expected in 2027. FDA filing discussions are ongoing, and an update is due this quarter.

items.headline: CVS to split into two public companies by 1H28 and raises 2026 EPS guidance to at least $8.20.
items.detail: The shares fell 12.5%. This is relevant to PBM and Caremark dynamics.

items.headline: US Treasury's proposed COINS Act biotech outbound-investment rule draws industry pushback.
items.detail: Critics say it is too broad. Comments are due 7 Dec, and RBC sees the China-data fears as overstated.

items.headline: Biora gets Australian ethics approval for a first-in-human trial of its BioJet oral adalimumab capsule.
items.detail: Dosing starts in December, with PK data expected in early 2027.
